instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Event venue and catering company managing a conference center and 3 satellite event spaces. Hosting 500+ corporate events and weddings annually. Looking to implement end-to-end event management software covering CRM, floor plan design, menu customization, and day-of operations coordination. We operate across multiple geographies and business units with a matrix organizational structure. A centralized digital transformation office coordinates innovation initiatives, but business unit autonomy means adoption varies significantly. Annual capex budget for innovation exists but deployment is gated by rigorous ROI modeling and steering committee approval.
answers.pastInitiatives: We piloted a cloud-based project management tool last year, but adoption was inconsistent across teams and we ultimately reverted to spreadsheets and email for most project tracking. The experience highlighted that tool adoption requires more structured change management than we initially planned for.
answers.strategicGoals: Customer retention has declined from 92% to 84% over the past 18 months, primarily among our mid-tier and enterprise segments. Exit interviews consistently cite product stagnation and poor digital self-service tools as reasons for leaving. We need to urgently modernize our customer-facing technology and proactively address the specific pain points driving churn before the trend becomes irreversible.
answers.teamSize: Innovation is decentralized across business units, each with its own innovation lead and dedicated resources, coordinated by a group-level Chief Innovation Officer. The total innovation workforce is approximately 100 people across the organization. A group innovation fund of €5M annually is allocated competitively — business units pitch for funding against clear innovation KPIs including revenue from new products and process efficiency gains.
answers.additionalContext: We underwent a significant restructuring 6 months ago, consolidating 5 business units into 3 and reducing headcount by 12%. The remaining teams are stretched thin managing the same workload with fewer people. Morale has stabilized but is still recovering. Any innovation initiative must be achievable without adding burden to already-overloaded teams and should visibly improve their daily work experience.

input.changes_since_last: Acquired 2 new enterprise clients. Expanded into adjacent market. Digital maturity improving.

opportunities.title: Develop Unified Digital Self-Service Portal (Customer Experience)
opportunities.rationale: The decline in customer retention is directly tied to poor digital self-service and product stagnation. Modernizing a centralized portal (CRM, booking, resource management) is critical for market defense. This effort must focus on empowering the *customer* first, making it less burdensome than full back-end system overhauls.

first_actions: Map current customer journey pain points specifically related to booking and post-event follow-up.
Define MVP scope focusing solely on the top 3 churn triggers (e.g., floor plan viewing, menu customization, basic inquiry).
Establish a formal feedback loop with the enterprise client base to guide feature prioritization.
execution_plan.success_metric: Increase in digital self-service adoption rate by 15% within 6 months.
milestones: Completion of detailed customer journey map and pain point prioritization.
Finalized wireframes for MVP portal (sign-off from Steering Committee).
Beta launch with the two acquired enterprise clients.

opportunities.title: Standardize Core Operational Workflows (Process Efficiency)
opportunities.rationale: The reliance on spreadsheets and email indicates significant process fragmentation, hindering scalability post-restructuring. Implementing a standardized, low-code workflow framework (e.g., centralized BPM tool) can improve efficiency without requiring massive IT overhaul, directly addressing the 'time' and 'strategy' barriers.

first_actions: Select 1-2 high-volume, currently spreadsheet-managed processes (e.g., vendor selection, booking confirmation) for initial pilot.
Conduct workshops with BUs to document current state workflows and identify mandatory compliance steps.
Train a small core group of 'Process Champions' within the remaining teams to drive localized adoption.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in manual time spent on pilot processes by 25%.
milestones: Successful mapping and documentation of the first two target workflows.
Piloting the automated workflow with positive user feedback (measured efficiency gain).
Formal adoption guidelines distributed to all remaining BU leads.

next_steps.action: Host a dedicated 'Process Standardization Workshop' involving operational leads to move critical workflows out of spreadsheets and into low-code tools, minimizing burden on staff.

Establish a formal 'Voice of Customer' task force with the marketing and enterprise sales teams to synthesize feedback data and create immediate, high-visibility tech improvements for mid-tier clients.
Review the innovation fund allocation process to explicitly mandate a minimum percentage budget dedicated to 'Staff Resilience & Efficiency' initiatives, acknowledging current staffing strain.

key_weaknesses: Persistent process fragmentation and reliance on manual/email workflows (hinders scalability).
Inconsistent digital adoption across business units, despite central CDTO efforts.
High systemic risk due to staff burnout and resource strain following recent restructuring.

improvements: Successfully acquired two new enterprise clients and expanded into an adjacent market segment.
Increased general awareness of the necessity for digital self-service, driven by internal failure analysis.
persistent_gaps: Failed implementation history (PM tool) has dampened team confidence in adopting large, centralized technology solutions.
The core pain point—customer retention decline among mid-tier clients—remains unaddressed by current foundational digital tools.
achieved_milestones: Completion of initial scoping for the workflow standardization pilot (Step 1).

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Improved client acquisition and market expansion provide external validation; however, the internal reality shows significant process debt, resource constraint post-restructuring, and an urgent need to modernize customer-facing tech.
